problem: The velocity of a particle is $(5i-3j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Final Velocity of a Particle
examples.problem: The velocity of a particle is $(\mathbf{i} -4\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\textrm{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}) \, \textrm{m/s}^2,$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=5 \, \textrm{s}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{a}t,
$$

where $\mathbf{u}$ is the initial velocity, and $\mathbf{a}$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
\mathbf u = \mathbf{i} -4\mathbf{j}, \qquad \mathbf a = 2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} .
$$

Therefore, after $t = 5 \, \textrm{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(i-4j)+(2i+j)(5) \\  & =(i-4j)+(10i+5j) \\  & =(11i+j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
A particle moves with a constant velocity of $u=-20i\,\text{ft/s}.$ Find the speed of the particle.

$|u|=$
{{field-1}}$\,\text{ft/s}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The speed of a particle equals the magnitude of its velocity.

Therefore, the speed of the particle is

$$
\begin{aligned}|u| & =|-20i| \\  & =|-20| \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

feet per second.
